secLayers.d: Private endpoint only; public network access disabled; App Service VNet integration; no IP firewall exceptions
Microsoft Entra authentication only; the API uses a managed identity; separate least-privilege database users per module and for migrations; no standing human access (just-in-time elevation)

Always Encrypted on Aadhaar, Emirates ID, passport, ABHA and insurance member numbers; column master key usable only by the API identity, so database admins and Medvya staff see ciphertext
TLS 1.2+ (1.3 where supported), Encrypt=Strict connections, HSTS on all web endpoints
Row-level security predicate on tenant_id set through SESSION_CONTEXT per request, plus EF Core query filters; cross-tenant tests in CI
Dynamic data masking on phone, email and date of birth for support and reporting roles
Ledger tables for audit events, signed notes, consents and invoices; digests stored in immutable Blob Storage and verified on schedule
Azure SQL auditing to Log Analytics and immutable storage; Defender for SQL alerts on injection and anomalous access; alert on bulk reads and exports
Point-in-time restore (up to 35 days), long-term retention per country rule, backups kept in-country, monthly restore drill
Parameterised queries only (EF Core/Dapper), no dynamic SQL, input validation, rate limits, watermarked exports
Key Vault with RBAC, soft delete and purge protection; GitHub OIDC to Azure; no secrets in code or config files

feats.d: .NET 10 solution (ASP.NET Core API + BFF, React web apps), EF Core 10 migration bundles, Docker Compose with SQL Server locally. GitHub Actions runs build, .NET analyzers, unit and integration tests (Testcontainers), CodeQL, dependency and secret scanning on every pull request. Protected main; deploys only from tags.

Bicep for dev, staging and production in the launch country: App Service (Linux, .NET 10), Azure SQL Database behind a private endpoint with public access disabled, private Blob Storage, Key Vault with purge protection, Application Insights, Defender for Cloud. Budgets and cost alerts per environment. OIDC federation from GitHub; no stored cloud secrets.
Sign-in, MFA (TOTP and passkeys), recovery, idle timeout on shared clinic PCs, device/session revocation, invite acceptance.

Organisation → facility → membership. clinic_id on every clinic-owned row, enforced by an EF Core global query filter and Azure SQL row-level security (tenant set in SESSION_CONTEXT per request). One doctor can belong to several clinics through memberships.

Role-permission matrix from Foundations (solo doctor, doctor, receptionist, nurse, practice admin, care coordinator, patient) checked server-side by ASP.NET Core authorisation policies on every endpoint, independently of the UI. Explicit 403 screens.

Append-only record of every read and write of patient data, sign-in, export and permission change: actor, tenant, patient, purpose, time, IP. Stored in Azure SQL ledger tables so any tampering is detectable.
Medvya MUI theme and tokens, clinical status primitives, component states and microcopy from Handoff; light theme; WCAG 2.2 AA base; English, Hindi and Arabic (RTL) string pipeline.
Threat model, data map, DPIA draft (DPDP), record-retention map per country, ADR-001 stack decision, ADR-002 launch market.

Entra-only database authentication, API connects with a managed identity (no passwords anywhere), separate least-privilege database users per module and for migrations, Always Encrypted on national ID and insurance member columns, dynamic data masking for support roles, TDE with customer-managed key. Details in section 7b.

Every field classified (public, internal, personal, sensitive health, national ID); synthetic-only test data policy; SECURITY.md and code review rules; privileged access through just-in-time elevation only; offline break-glass account.

findings.t: Market-specific Musts gate UAE, not India
findings.d: Exchange connection, Emirates ID and eClaimLink are UAE launch blockers. If India launches first, they move within P5 without delaying the first paying clinic.
P-01 and C-01 are marked “next” rather than hi-fi in Foundations; confirm final designs before P1 and P4 build respectively.
